text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.4.b","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Share Theories and Reveal the Source activity, students learn the Greek root logy, compare bio + logy, and apply it to geology and zoology."},{"code":"RI.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Mystery Passages activity, groups annotate the three passages and answer the three inference questions using cited words and phrases as evidence."},{"code":"RI.6.4","verdict":"partly","reason":"The Read and Discuss and Mystery Passages activities teach using context clues and the word myth as used in the article, but no activity addresses figurative or connotative meanings."},{"code":"SL.6.1.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Read and Discuss activity, students read the article beforehand and use Turn and Talk to share a sentence as evidence, and the group discussions require citing text evidence."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The lesson uses the full \"What Are Myths?\" article and three Coolidge Prometheus/Pandora passages, but it leaves the passage selection to the teacher and names no specific pages."}}
